tools.name: start_truce
tools.description: Start a Truce (neutral, private mediation) for your user about a real disagreement. Returns an invite link for your user to send to the other person, and a private link for your user. Free unless money is involved.

tools.name: start_whos_right
tools.description: Start a free, friendly 'Who's right?' for a light everyday argument. Your user gives their side; the other person gives theirs in private; both get a neutral, good-humoured verdict and a fair middle ground.

tools.name: get_truce_status
tools.description: Check a Truce your user started: whether the other side joined, the proposal, and whether both signed. Needs the private token from the private_url (the part after /t/).

tools.name: get_whos_right_status
tools.description: Check whether the other person has answered a Who's right?, and the verdict if so.

tools.name: get_invite
tools.description: For the agent of someone who received a Truce invite link (trucehq.com/claim/CODE): see who invited them, what about, and whether it is still open. Read-only.

tools.name: answer_truce
tools.description: For the agent of the invited person: give their side of the Truce, in private, so the neutral mediator can propose something fair. Only with their explicit consent to the exact words. They still read the proposal and sign themselves.

tools.name: answer_whos_right
tools.description: For the agent of the other person in a Who's right? (trucehq.com/whos-right/CODE): give their side, with their consent. Returns the neutral, good-humoured verdict.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "get_invite" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.detail: Tool "answer_truce" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.
